rapport_notes: Joanna was friendly, conversational, used customer's name appropriately, and maintained a warm tone throughout the call.
process_discipline_notes: No silence held after open-ended questions; rep immediately re-pitched or moved forward after asking about concerns and special instructions.

evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep launched straight into confirming details ('calling to confirm the details of your upcoming move') with no time-boxed ask or framing of what would happen on the call in exchange for the customer's time.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked after logistics probing: 'So do you have any special instructions, concerns or stressors about moving in general that you want me to take note of at this time?' — this came after 10+ minutes of room-by-room inventory and parking logistics.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer mentioned concern about assembly/reassembly and not needing to be present. Rep answered assembly directly ('the guys can definitely help you with assembly reassembly') but did not probe deeper on the 'not needing to be present' concern beyond offering payment/contact note options. No second-layer follow-up like 'tell me more about why that's important' or 'what else is on your mind about the move.'
evidence_quotes.sheet1_careful_with: Covered in Stage 2 takeaway: 'we also include other features like our no worries damage coverage which would give you up to $2,000 coverage for any repair, replacement reimbursement for any accidental damages.'
evidence_quotes.sheet2_whos_coming: Covered in Stage 2 takeaway: 'Also meet your mover feature. So we'll send you the names of the guest ahead of time.'
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee: Covered in Stage 2 takeaway: 'lastly on time guarantee. If we run late, we provide discounts by the end of the day.'
evidence_quotes.communication: Never covered. No mention of day-before call, named crew lead contact, inbox updates, or any proactive communication protocol.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Full anchor provided with personalization: 'for one bedroom apartment usually can take two and a half to three and a half hours to complete the factor that we want to consider here are really the stairs. Since we have stairs on both locations so that might just add more time to the move itself.' Quoted 3–4 hour range personalized to stairs.
evidence_quotes.estimate_is_a_window: 'of course the Gus would be able to finish everything earlier than that, that's fine, you only pay for how long it will take after the twenty a half hour minimum is net. So the shorter to move the lower the cost.'
evidence_quotes.beats_it_pay_less: Same quote as above — 'you only pay for how long it will take' and 'the shorter to move the lower the cost.'
evidence_quotes.does_that_feel_fair_then_silence: Never asked. Rep moved directly into 'Okay. Alright, is there anything else I can help you out today?' with no fair-framing question or pause.
evidence_quotes.close_rate_lock: Never mentioned. No reference to when rate locks or booking protection.
evidence_quotes.close_explicit_ask: Implicit close ('should we expect you to be there') rather than explicit ask for the move. No clear 'would you like our help with your move' or equivalent.

top_strength: Joanna built strong rapport and managed a complex multi-floor inventory intake smoothly, asking clarifying questions and confirming critical logistics (stairs, parking, floor proximity) that directly informed the estimate.
coaching_note: Front-load the quid pro quo frame before probing, ask the agenda question before diving into logistics, and hold silence after open-ended questions — these three moves unlock the customer's real concerns and set up Stage 2 differentiators properly.
